message.content: **Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and decided to buy. The fundamentals support a modest long position: total net sales grew 2% to $391.0 billion, driven by Services up 13% to $96.2 billion, with total gross margin expanding to 46.2% from 44.1% and operating income rising to $123.2 billion from $114.3 billion. Net income of $93.7 billion and diluted EPS of $6.08 were slightly below FY2023 ($97.0 billion / $6.13) solely because of a one-time $10.2 billion net tax charge tied to the EU State Aid Decision, which lifted the effective tax rate to 24.1% from 14.7% — an accounting item, not an operating deterioration. Cash generation remains exceptional at $118.3 billion in operating cash flow, funding $95.0 billion of buybacks and $15.2 billion of dividends while still leaving $140.8 billion in cash and marketable securities. The main soft spots are Greater China net sales down 8% to $67.0 billion and continued weakness in iPad and Wearables, plus ongoing DOJ/EU DMA antitrust exposure. On that basis I placed one buy order for 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.90, against a quote of $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), which filled at $222.90 for a total of about $9,808 — within the $10,000 per-order cap, well under the $20,000 daily total, and funded entirely from the $50,000 cash balance with no money moved out of the account.
